summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with HCV-related cirrhosis and multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma, was readmitted two days after discharge due to fever, chills, and new bruising at the RFA site. He was diagnosed with post-RFA syndrome with reactive pleural effusion and a small pulmonary infiltrate concerning for mild pneumonia. He was treated with a short course of levofloxacin and received albumin for hyponatremia (Na 127). His symptoms resolved, inflammatory markers improved, and he remained hemodynamically stable. He was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor the bruising, and follow up with labs and a repeat chest X-ray.
